clue.text: Swell dance circle working

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
O is circle-shaped
on means operating or working, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A round dance gets going and the circle of dancers spreads out.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to inflate or expand, just as a rubber bag filled with air grows larger.

clue.text: Reportedly prohibited joker having as topic fashionable movement

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so a word that sounds like the synonym is entered

parts.note: prohibited means banned
a wag is a joker or wit
on means about, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: A comedian banned from performing builds an act around the latest trend.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNED said aloud gives BAND, the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping on the bandwagon means joining a popular trend, so the word names a craze or fashionable cause.

clue.text: Start short date with posh fellow

indicators.note: short means the synonym is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: to date someone is to see them romantically
a toff is an upper-class man

explanation.surface: A brief romantic evening out with an upper-class gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-off is a starting point or beginning, as in setting off on a journey.

clue.text: Most heated feeling of dread about boundless grief

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anxious word goes round the other piece

parts.note: angst is a feeling of anxiety or dread

indicators.note: boundless means without its edges, so the outer letters of grief go

explanation.surface: Endless grief brings on a terrible, fiery dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated describes temper running high, so the superlative means the most furious.

clue.text: Farmer, a good country-dweller, welcomes international school

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the rural word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a ruralist lives in or favours the countryside
a cult is a school of thought or following

explanation.surface: A kindly rural farmer plays host to a school from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: ICULT goes in after the first R of RURALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who practises agriculture, growing crops or rearing livestock, is a farmer.

clue.text: Swimmer ultimately recognising mature following is hot!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of recognising

parts.note: old means mature in years
F is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. ff.
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a mature fan base makes something cool, or rather hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small orange carp kept in bowls and ponds is a fish, a swimmer by crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Country's supporter half-heartedly supporting computer technology

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the other piece

parts.note: IT is information technology

indicators.note: half-heartedly means losing half the heart, one of the two middle letters

parts.note: an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A nation's champion gives only lukewarm backing to its tech sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country's' is the definition plus 'is'; in a down light the supporting piece sits underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean nation with Rome as capital is a country.

clue.text: Refusal to speak of riotous license

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of license are thrown about

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about wild, unrestrained behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mute, saying nothing at all, is a refusal to talk.

clue.text: Leave vet interminably holding a pet

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the shortened word goes round the rest
interminably means without end, so the last letter of vet goes

parts.note: a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: A vet keeps hold of someone's cat while the owner leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a room or premises is to vacate it, emptying it.

clue.text: Engineers likely to be trustworthy

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
liable means likely, as in liable to happen

explanation.surface: A claim that engineers can generally be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dependable that can be counted on is trustworthy.

clue.text: Pleased with oil I cooked up for plants

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: cooked up means concocted, so the letters of oil I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener delighted with a homemade oil for the flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall flowering members of the iris family, the sword lilies, are plants.

clue.text: Somewhat gruffly in general quitting hurriedly

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone leaving abruptly with a rather gruff manner overall.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying off means dashing away, leaving in a great hurry.

clue.text: Doubtfully ate up mostly foul stew

indicators.note: doubtfully suggests uncertain order, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of foul goes

explanation.surface: A diner reluctantly finishes a nasty-tasting stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims foul to FOU, and 'Doubtfully' rearranges ATEUP with FOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The French dish of boiled beef and vegetables is a classic slow-cooked casserole.

clue.text: Auditor finally hears half of text on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside a vessel, so the pieces go inside the ship word

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of hears
half of takes the first two of the four letters of text

explanation.surface: An auditor at last hears part of a message read aloud aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditor in its root sense is a hearer, someone attending to sound.

clue.text: Inquiring into pound invested in public showing by clique

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the money sign goes into the show word

parts.note: an expo is a public exhibition
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
a ring is a closed group or clique

explanation.surface: A probe into money sunk into a public exhibition by a cabal.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigating a subject, looking into it closely, is examining or probing it.

clue.text: Novice with inclination for dialect of German

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
a lean is a slant or tendency

explanation.surface: A beginner with a leaning towards a regional German tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The speech of the Tyrol, the Alpine region of Austria and Italy, is a German dialect.

clue.text: Some get hanky out as response to present situation

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people reach for a tissue when moved by the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present situation' means being given a present, not the current state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of gratitude are the natural reply on receiving a gift.

clue.text: Season's yield — unusual haste to gather in right volume

indicators.note: to gather in means to take inside, so the shuffled letters surround the others
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of haste are rearranged

explanation.surface: Farmers rush unusually to bring in the crop before the season ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes HAEST from haste; RV goes in after HA.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop gathered in at the end of a growing season is its yield.

clue.text: King, troublesome fellow, acquired knowledge

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
a ned is a Scottish slang term for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: A king, a difficult man, becomes educated.
explanation.walkthrough: NED is Scots slang for a young tearaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb meaning to study and gain skill is to have acquired knowledge.

clue.text: Grass protecting ring broke with established customs

indicators.note: protecting means shielding round, so the grass word encloses the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a bell gives a ring

explanation.surface: Grass wrapped round a ring breaks with tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a verb, to inform, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising against authority or convention means defying the established order.

clue.text: British at last go teetotal before the Parisian drinking bout

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of go

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Briton finally goes on the wagon before a French binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the jar, a spell of heavy drinking, is a session on the booze.

clue.text: Picture of old cold farm worker returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the joined pieces read backwards

parts.note: a serf was a feudal farm labourer

explanation.surface: A painting of an old farmhand coming home in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: OCSERF read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall painting done on wet plaster is a type of picture.

clue.text: Work hastily and superficially read page

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly and superficially

explanation.surface: Slapdash work: a page read only lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superficially' looks like part of the definition but belongs with 'read'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp on effort, doing a job in a rushed, careless way, is to work hastily.

clue.text: Rarely it could be associated with writing

indicators.note: could be means one possible arrangement, so the letters of Rarely it are reordered

explanation.surface: A wry remark that something is rarely to do with books.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to books, authors and written works is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Disease in fruit recurring we hear

indicators.note: recurring means happening again, so the piece appears twice
we hear means spoken aloud, so a word sounding like the fruit is used

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: An illness caught repeatedly from fruit, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: BERRY spoken gives BERI, said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A thiamine deficiency causing nerve and heart trouble is a tropical illness.

clue.text: Hang around and fake illness when mum goes

indicators.note: goes means departs, so the word for mother is removed

parts.note: to malinger is to feign sickness
ma is an informal word for mum

explanation.surface: A child loiters and pretends to be ill once mother has left.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter, staying on longer than needed, is to hang around.

clue.text: Move fast! Don't do this with something unpleasant!

definitions.meaning: an order to hurry up, put your foot down

definitions.text: Don't do this with something unpleasant!
definitions.meaning: advice to avoid treading on, for instance, dog mess in the street

explanation.surface: Hurry up, but watch where you tread on the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means accelerate, and literally means to tread upon something.
